question.problem:
The Taylor series for the function $f(x)$ about $x=0$ is given by

$$
f(x)={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n-1}}{n!}{x}^{n}.
$$

The series converges to $f(x)$ for $|x|<R,$ where $R$ is the radius of convergence of the Taylor series. Calculate the radius of convergence of the Taylor series expansion of ${f}^{′}(x),$ the derivative of $f(x),$ about $x=0.$
question.worked_solution:
The radius of convergence for the Taylor series of ${f}^{′}(x)$ is the same as the Taylor series of $f(x).$ So, to find the radius of convergence of ${f}^{′}(x),$ we need to compute $R.$ 

To calculate $R,$ we can use the ratio test. Computing the limit of the absolute value of the ratio of two consecutive terms, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{{a}_{n+1}}{{a}_{n}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{(-1)^{n}{x}^{n+1}}{(n+1)!}\cdot \frac{n!}{(-1)^{n-1}{x}^{n}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{(-1)x\cdot n!}{(n+1)!}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{|x|}{n+1} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

The series converges when $L<1.$  Since $0<1$ for all $x,$ we conclude that 
$R=\infty .$
